name: custom
description: Your own deploy: AWS, a self-hosted box, any script. A synced workflow runs your deploy command, creates the GitHub deployment, verifies the new build is serving, and posts the terminal status the production gate waits for.
notes: Hosts like Vercel and Railway post a GitHub deployment_status themselves; a deploy you run does not, so the post-deploy gate would never fire. deploy-custom.yml fills that gap: it creates the GitHub deployment, runs deploy_command, verifies, posts success or failure, then dispatches post-deploy-prod.yml (a status created with GITHUB_TOKEN does not trigger other workflows).

deploy_command (sdlc-config.json) is run with bash on the runner at the deployed commit. It receives DEPLOY_SHA, DEPLOY_ENVIRONMENT and PROD_URL, plus every secret named in deploy_secrets as an environment variable (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, an SSH key, ...). Keep it idempotent; exit non-zero to fail the deployment.

Set deployed_sha_url (and deployed_sha_jq, e.g. .version.sha) to an endpoint that reports the running commit: verification then proves the NEW build is serving. Without it only a health check runs, which an old build still answering also passes.
deploy_trigger: push_to_main (default) deploys on every push to the release branch, git_tag on pushed v* tags, manual only on workflow_dispatch.
No reconcile capability: this workflow records the GitHub deployment itself, so there is no webhook to lose. Self-hosted runners: set runner in sdlc-config.json as for any host.
